title: Finite-type special-neutral open subgroup and its strict-local translates
statement:
Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $L$, residue field $k$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $J/T$ be a smooth separated group scheme locally of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; its multiplication, identity and inverse satisfy the group diagrams, and separated means that its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Suppose $J_L$ is of finite type [def-pc-base-change]. Let $J_k^0$ be the connected component containing the identity in the special fibre, with its open-subscheme structure; connected components mean maximal connected subsets [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then
$$U=J\setminus(J_k\setminus J_k^0)$$
is an open subgroup scheme [def-weil-open-immersion], smooth, separated and of finite type over $A$, with $U_L=J_L$ and $U_k=J_k^0$. For every field extension $k'/k$, $(J_k^0)_{k'}=(J_{k'})^0$. If $B\to A$ is a faithfully flat homomorphism of discrete valuation rings [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map] and $J$ carries a group-compatible descent datum $\alpha$ relative to $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-pd-descent-datum], then $\alpha(p_0^*U)=p_1^*U$ on $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_BA)$. If $A$ is strictly henselian [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], the translates $\lambda U$ for sections $\lambda\in J(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_T(T,J)$ cover $J$. Here $\lambda U$ is the image of the open immersion obtained by left multiplication by $\lambda$. No quasi-compactness of $J$ or Neron mapping property is assumed.

source.place: Raynaud, Specialisation du foncteur de Picard, printed pp.40-42: (3.2)(d), (3.3.4) definition of G^{00}, and the translate-cover paragraph in the smooth sketch of (3.3.1). Finite-type assertion is the agent specialization to finite-type generic fibre (two quasi-compact fibres). Primary scan read online at https://numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1970__38__27_0.pdf; local PDF WANTED. No SGA result is cited as an input.

proof.text: By local-finite-type base change, $J_k$ is locally of finite type over $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-lft-field-group-neutral-component] to this group: its identity component $C=J_k^0$ is clopen and of finite type, is a subgroup with the open-subscheme structure, and satisfies $C_{k'}=(J_{k'})^0$ for every field extension $k'/k$. This proves the requested field-extension clause without any perfectness assumption. The smooth-fibre clause of [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion] also shows that $J_k$ is smooth over $k$.

source.place: Tag 0B7R, proposition-connected-component; local finite type by morphisms.tex Tag 01T4; smooth fibres in Tag 01VB, as recorded by sbc-lem-smooth-criterion.

proof.text: The subset $J_k$ is closed in $J$: on an affine chart it is cut out by a uniformizer of $A$. Since $C$ is clopen in $J_k$, $J_k\setminus C$ is closed in $J$, so its complement $U$ is open. The open-subscheme restriction gives $U_L=J_L$ and $U_k=C$, with their actual scheme structures. Multiplication of $U\times_TU$ lands in $U$: over the generic point there is no restriction, and over the closed point it is multiplication in the subgroup $C$. The same check works for inverse and identity. The open factorization lemma supplies the restricted morphisms. Their group diagrams hold because they hold after the open inclusion into $J$, a monomorphism. Restriction of a smooth morphism to an open is smooth. The diagonal of $U/T$ is the pullback of the closed diagonal of $J/T$ to $U\times_TU$, so it is a closed immersion. Thus $U/T$ is smooth and separated.

source.place: Elementary open-complement and group-diagram argument using the special-fibre identity subgroup; Raynaud (3.3.4), printed p.42, motivates this construction (local PDF WANTED). Restriction uses morphisms.tex Tags 01VA and 01VC; closed diagonals use Tag 01JY.

proof.text: For any open cover of $U$, restricting to $U_L=J_L$ gives a finite subfamily covering that fibre, since $J_L$ is of finite type. Restricting to $U_k=C$ gives another finite subfamily, since Step 1 gives finite type of $C$. These two finite subfamilies cover every point of $U$, as $\operatorname{Spec}A$ has only its generic and closed points: by uniformizer factorization, any nonzero prime contains the uniformizer and hence equals the maximal ideal. Hence $U$ is quasi-compact. Smoothness gives local finite presentation; an algebra with a finite presentation is generated by its finitely many displayed variables. Thus $U/T$ is locally of finite type, and the only nonempty opens of this trait are the whole trait and its generic point, whose inverse images are the quasi-compact spaces $U$ and $J_L$. Thus $U/T$ is quasi-compact as a morphism and is of finite type by definition. This uses neither quasi-compactness of $J$ nor a Neron mapping property.

source.place: Tag 01T1, definition-finite-type, applied directly to the two quasi-compact fibres; elementary finite-subcover argument written by Q01.

proof.text: Now let $B\to A$ be faithfully flat. It is injective: tensoring the injection $bB\hookrightarrow B$ with the flat $B$-module $A$ remains injective; if $b$ maps to zero, its source $bB\otimes_BA$ is zero, and faithfulness forces $bB=0$. A uniformizer $\pi_B$ cannot become a unit, since otherwise the nonzero module $B/\pi_BB$ would tensor to zero. For a uniformizer $\pi_A$, the DVR factorization theorem therefore gives $\pi_B=u\pi_A^r$ in $A$ for a unit $u$ and integer $r\geq1$. In $D=A\otimes_BA$, write $a_0=\pi_A\otimes1$ and $a_1=1\otimes\pi_A$. The common image of $\pi_B$ is a unit times $a_i^r$ for either $i$. For every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $D$ this implies $a_0\in\mathfrak q$ if and only if $a_1\in\mathfrak q$. Consequently $p_0$ and $p_1$ send each point of $\operatorname{Spec}D$ to the same point (closed or generic) of $\operatorname{Spec}A$.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, uniformizer factorization; faithful-flatness consequences proved directly from the tensor-exactness definition. This is the ramified-overlap calculation written by Q01.

proof.text: For a point $q\in\operatorname{Spec}D$, put $F=\kappa(q)$. If its two images are generic, both $(p_i^*U)_F$ are the whole respective group fibre. If its two images are closed, the two maps $k\to F$ can differ; nevertheless Step 1, applied with each map separately, identifies $(p_i^*U)_F$ with the identity component of $(p_i^*J)_F$. Since the descent isomorphism $\alpha$ respects the group operations, it preserves identity. Its underlying homeomorphism therefore carries one identity component onto the other, by maximality of connected components and the inverse homeomorphism. Thus $\alpha$ identifies the two open subsets on every residue-field fibre. Every point of the total space lies in such a fibre, so the underlying opens agree. The structure sheaf of an open subscheme is the restriction of the ambient structure sheaf; consequently the equality is one of open subschemes, $\alpha(p_0^*U)=p_1^*U$, even if $D$ is nonreduced.

source.place: Tag 023V, definition-descent-datum; fibrewise characterization from Step 1 and the simultaneous generic/special alternatives of Step 4. No effectiveness theorem or unramifiedness is used.

proof.text: Assume $A$ strictly henselian, so $k$ is separably closed and $(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ is henselian. For $x\in J_k$, the fibre-component-neighbourhood lemma applied to $J_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ gives a nonempty open $W$ containing $x$ and contained in its connected component. Since $J_k$ is smooth, density of $J_k(k)$ supplies $g\in W(k)$. Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}E\subset J$ containing the image of $g$. The restriction $V\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is smooth, hence $E$ is a smooth $A$-algebra by the affine smoothness comparison. Since $g:\operatorname{Spec}k\to J$ lands in $V$, it factors uniquely through $V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], and by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] this factorization over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an $A$-algebra map $E\to A/\mathfrak m_A=k$. Apply henselian smooth-algebra lifting with $R=A$, $S=E$, the target algebra $A$, and $I=\mathfrak m_A$. It gives an $A$-algebra map $E\to A$, which by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] is a morphism $T\to V$ over $T$, hence a section $\lambda:T\to V\subset J$ specializing to $g$. The source algebra is smooth and finitely presented; neither $J$ nor its whole special fibre was assumed quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0H74, lemma-lift-smooth-henselian; varieties.tex Tag 056U, lemma-smooth-separable-closed-points-dense (separably closed case); topology.tex Tags 04MF/04ME for component neighbourhoods.

proof.text: Left multiplication $L_\lambda:J\to J$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $L_{\lambda^{-1}}$: their composites are the identity by associativity and the inverse law. Thus $\lambda U$ is open. On the special fibre $L_g$ sends the identity component $C$ onto the component of $g$: each inclusion follows by connectedness and maximality, applying $L_g$ and then $L_{g^{-1}}$. Since $g$ and $x$ in Step 6 lie in the same component, $x\in(\lambda U)_k$. This covers all special-fibre points. Every generic-fibre point is already in $U$, the translate by the identity section, since $U_L=J_L$. Therefore the translates by all sections cover $J$.
